name: Packaging cleanroom contamination
blurb: Business interruption at advanced packaging facilities affected by airborne particulates.
summary: Business interruption at advanced packaging facilities affected by airborne particulates.

part_3_high_value_red_flags: A broad contamination exclusion that defines contamination to include any airborne particulate, regardless of source, would eliminate coverage for the core exposure.
An absolute pollution exclusion that applies to indoor air quality or particulates released inside the cleanroom would bar most contamination claims.
A wear and tear or gradual deterioration exclusion that treats filter loading or particle accumulation as expected maintenance rather than a covered loss.
A faulty workmanship or design error exclusion that applies to the cleanroom HVAC or filtration system would defeat coverage for the most common cause of contamination.
A business interruption waiting period longer than 72 hours would leave the insured bearing the full cost of short but frequent contamination shutdowns.
A sublimit for decontamination and recertification costs below the actual cost of cleaning a Class 1 or Class 10 cleanroom would leave a large uninsured gap.
An exclusion for loss due to failure of air handling or filtration equipment unless caused by a named peril such as fire or windstorm would not respond to mechanical breakdown or power surge.
manuscript_wording_and_carve_backs: Amend the definition of contamination to expressly include airborne particulates of any size, including submicron particles, regardless of source.
Delete or narrow the absolute pollution exclusion so it does not apply to particulates released inside the cleanroom from normal operations or equipment failure.
Add affirmative coverage for decontamination, recertification, and revalidation of the cleanroom to the required ISO class after a particulate event.
Add coverage for business interruption caused by failure of HVAC, filtration, or air handling equipment due to mechanical breakdown, electrical surge, or operator error.
Add coverage for loss due to ingress of outside air during construction, maintenance, or filter changeout, including dust and pollen.
Add coverage for contingent business interruption from loss of a key supplier of ultrapure water, process gases, or specialty chemicals used in packaging.
Add a manuscript endorsement that removes any sublimit for cleanroom decontamination and instead pays actual costs up to the property limit.

part_4_program_structure_and_limits.bi_waiting_period: A waiting period of 24 to 72 hours is typical for contamination related business interruption, with 48 hours common for cleanroom particulate events because decontamination and recertification often exceed one day.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.business_interruption: Business interruption is usually written on a gross earnings form with a 12 to 24 month extended period of indemnity, and contingent business interruption for key suppliers of substrates, chemicals, and gases is often sublimited to $5 million to $10 million.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.property_eb_equipment: Equipment breakdown coverage is typically written with a sublimit of $10 million to $25 million for HVAC, filtration, and air handling units, but higher sublimits are negotiable for critical cleanroom systems.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.per_occurrence_primary_excess_layered_pr: Primary property layer typically carries $25 million to $50 million per occurrence, with excess layers in $50 million to $100 million increments up to the total insurable value of the building, cleanroom, and production equipment.

part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.cgl_primary: Typical primary commercial general liability limit is $1 million per occurrence and $2 million general aggregate, but higher limits are often required by customer contracts.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.paper_basis: Occurrence based for third party liability because a contamination event is a sudden and identifiable incident, while first party property and business interruption respond on a loss occurring during the policy period basis.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.excess_umbrella_towers: Excess and umbrella towers typically add $5 million to $25 million in layers, with total limits driven by contractual indemnity requirements and the value of downstream customer losses.

part_1_core_third_party_liability_exposu: Product liability if contaminated packaged chips are shipped to customers and later fail in end devices, causing property damage or bodily injury.
Contractual liability to customers for late delivery or nonconforming product under supply agreements that include liquidated damages or warranty penalties.
Pollution liability if airborne particulates or cleaning chemicals are released outside the facility and cause damage to neighboring properties or the environment.
Completed operations liability if contamination is discovered after the packaged chips leave the facility and cause failures in downstream assembly or end use.
Errors and omissions liability for failure to detect or report contamination that leads to customer losses, if the facility provides testing or certification services.
Employers liability if employees suffer respiratory or other injuries from exposure to particulates or cleaning agents during decontamination.
Third party property damage if contamination spreads through shared ventilation or utility connections to adjacent tenant spaces in a building with multiple occupants.

underwriter_wants_to_know: What ISO cleanroom class does the packaging area maintain and what is the maximum allowable particle count per cubic meter for the critical process steps.
What are the specific sources of airborne particulates in the facility, such as personnel, equipment, materials, or outside air, and how are they controlled.
What real time particle monitoring and alarm systems are in place, and what is the response time from detection to isolation of the affected tool or area.
What is the historical frequency and severity of cleanroom contamination events at this facility and at comparable advanced packaging sites.
What is the maximum probable loss from a single contamination event, including product scrap, decontamination, recertification, and business interruption downtime.
What redundancy exists for HVAC, filtration, and air handling units, and can the cleanroom maintain class during maintenance or filter changeout.
What contractual obligations to customers require guaranteed uptime or penalties for delayed shipments of packaged chips.
